**Rating:** ★ 4.7 (out of 5) - **Reviews:** 1,012 written reviews (1,291 total ratings) — well above the 30-review threshold - **Source:** https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/212721/indian-chicken-curry-murgh-kari/ - **Author / Updated by:** Ayshren; updated September 11, 2026 (tested by the Allrecipes Test Kitchen) - **Servings:** 6 ## Preparation & Cooking Time - **Prep Time:** 20 minutes - **Cook Time:** 40 minutes - **Total Time:** 1 hour ## Ingredients (1× serving = 6) 1. 2 pounds skinless, boneless chicken breast halves 2. 2 teaspoons salt 3. 3 tablespoons cooking oil, or as needed 4. 1½ cups chopped onion 5. 1 tablespoon minced garlic 6. 1½ teaspoons minced fresh ginger root 7. 1 tablespoon curry powder 8. 1 teaspoon ground cumin 9. 1 teaspoon ground turmeric 10. 1 teaspoon ground coriander 11. 1 teaspoon cayenne pepper 12. 1 tablespoon water 13. 1 (15 ounce) can crushed tomatoes 14. 1 cup plain yogurt 15. 1 tablespoon chopped fresh cilantro 16. 1 teaspoon salt 17. ½ cup water 18. 1 teaspoon garam masala 19. 1 tablespoon chopped fresh cilantro 20. 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice ## Cooking Instructions 1. **Gather all ingredients.** 2. **Season and brown the chicken:** Sprinkle the chicken breasts with 2 teaspoons salt. Heat 1–2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over high heat. Brown chicken in batches (adding more oil as needed) until partially cooked and golden on all sides. Transfer browned chicken to a plate and set aside. 3. **Sauté aromatics:** Reduce heat to medium. Add the onion, garlic, and ginger to the oil left in the skillet. Cook and stir until the onion is soft and translucent, 5–8 minutes. Stir in curry powder, cumin, turmeric, coriander, cayenne, and 1 tablespoon of water; cook together about 1 minute, stirring constantly. 4. **Build the sauce:** Add the crushed tomatoes, yogurt, 1 tablespoon chopped cilantro, and 1 teaspoon salt; stir to combine. 5. **Simmer the curry:** Return the chicken breasts (with any juices on the plate) to the skillet. Pour in ½ cup water and bring to a boil, turning the chicken to coat in the sauce. Sprinkle the garam masala and 1 tablespoon cilantro over the chicken. 6. **Finish cooking:** Cover and simmer until the chicken is no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, about 20 minutes (an instant-read thermometer should read at least 165 °F / 74 °C). 7. **Serve:** Drizzle with fresh lemon juice and enjoy. ### Recipe Notes / Tips - Boneless chicken thighs can be substituted for chicken breasts. - Coconut milk can replace the yogurt if preferred. - Leftovers keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days — reheat gently over low heat.
